Carlos (AcmeOps): Hey team — we're getting lots of 429s right at the top of each minute for a single API key. It's consistent every minute for a 5–10s window. No deploys. :frowning:
Anna (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste a small curl and the response headers you're seeing? also which region+endpoint?
Carlos (AcmeOps): eu-west /v1/generate, example response headers: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, no `X-RateLimit` headers present, body: `{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}`. Using our app server pool -> single API key shared across ~25 backend workers.
Anna (Support): thanks — do you see `Retry-After` at all? can you run a quick 60s window capture so we can see exact timestamps? :eyes:
Carlos (AcmeOps): no Retry-After. here's a quick repro loop we ran: ```for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done``` It reliably triggers first second of each minute.
Mike (eng-oncall): pinging eng-runtime. initial look at the proxy logs for that key shows a tight cluster of connections being reused and requests concatenated around `:00` every minute. looks like our connection pooling + client's sync wakes up caused a minute-aligned burst. :thinking_face:
Priya (sre): that pattern screams synchronized cron/synthetic checks or pooled workers that jitter in the same clock boundary. do you run any NewRelic / Datadog synthetic pings or minutely cron jobs from your infra?
Carlos (AcmeOps): aha — yes we recently enabled NewRelic synthetics every minute for health-checking the path. didn't think that would align with 25 workers but we do have request fanout on the health check.
Anna (Support): ok that explains synchronized spikes. quick mitigation options:
- disable/minimize synthetics or change to random jitter (recommended)
- add `backoff + jitter` on your client retry loop and spread health checks across different offsets
- we can temporarily raise RPM for your org while you change the checks (requires billing/ops approval)
Mike (eng-oncall): technical detail — our rate limiter is token-bucket per API key with a per-minute refill that is applied in a single tick internally. if many tokens get consumed in the same refill tick the instantaneous RPM can blow past the steady-state expectation and hit the per-second enforcement causing 429 windows. we're working on a smoother refill but for now client-side spreading helps a lot.
Priya (sre): reproduction steps for eng-runtime (what I used):
```bash
# from a linux box, simulate 25 workers and a synthetic check aligned to top of minute
for i in $(seq 1 25); do (while :; do sleep $(( (60 - $(date +%s) % 60) )); for j in {1..4}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; done; sleep 60; done) & done
# will show burst right after sleep alignment
```
Mike (eng-oncall): notes for runtime team: consider short-term server-side smoothing: spread the refill across a sliding window, add micro-token pacing for refill tick, and emit `X-RateLimit-*` headers even on 429s so clients can adapt. filing ENG-9812 with logs attached.
Anna (Support): action items for support:
- Carlos: try disabling NewRelic synthetics or add jitter and confirm if the minute-window goes away (if you want we can coordinate a short maintenance window)
- Support: if customer wants immediate relief, offer to provision temporary +20% RPM for 24h while they change checks (requires billing sign-off)
- Eng: prioritize header visibility and smoothing options (per Mike)
Carlos (AcmeOps): will try disabling synthetics now and report back. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ratebot: Incident note created: INC-2026-431 - "minute-aligned client burst -> 429 windows"
Anna (Support): follow-up — if the customer sees improvement, we'll close this thread. if not, we'll need a packet-level capture and proxy connection logs (eng to advise).
Carlos (AcmeOps): turned off the synthetics and added 30s jitter, initial run looks clean — no minute spikes at top-of-minute. will monitor for 2 hours and report. thanks team.
Mike (eng-oncall): great. I'll keep ENG-9812 open for smoothing work; adding `emit-rate-headers` as a subtask. :white_check_mark:
